summary:
IPSEITY's market layer is one AMM per NFT inside a single contract (src/Pool.sol), keyed by token id, where ownerOf(id) is the sole liquidity provider and the only authority: selling the NFT sells the exchange (reserves, fee income, curve) with no LP shares, no migration, no wrapper. Pricing is constant product with anchored virtual reserves (x+vx)(y+vy)=k; the offsets vBase/vQuote are stored on the market and written only by openMarket/deposit/withdraw/syncCurve, never by a trade (a derived-per-quote version leaked 400 in -> 718 out at 8x concentration and was caught by tools/fuzz.mjs). Concentration (0..80,000 bps) is a deterministic function of the token's 256-bit 4-D section word via lib/Curve.sol (cut-plane normal u=R·e_w, per-solid SLICE/FALLOFF tables measured off the engine), copied into the market only when the holder calls syncCurve so an ERC-4907 renter cannot reprice someone else's inventory. A ratcheting bond (bondUntil only moves out, <= 365 days, survives transfer) freezes every exit and every term while additive operations (deposit, trade) stay open; withdrawal can never be paused; the five admin switches provably take no token id or amount. Every transfer is measured (fee-on-transfer safe on both sides, minOut checked against what the recipient actually received); no single trade may take more than half the real outgoing reserve; an enumerable open-market set replaces an indexer.

The launchpad (src/Kiln.sol) deploys ownerless fixed-supply ERC-20s (Coin) by CREATE2 with the sender mixed into the salt, mines Uniswap v4 hook salts inside a view (Kiln.mine) so a browser with no keccak can deploy a hook under eth_call, refuses to hand back a hook whose address bits do not equal its declared permissions (WrongFlags), and ships two hooks: Gate (trading opens at OPENS, liquidity locked until UNLOCKS, both immutable; beforeSwap + beforeRemoveLiquidity) and Facet (dynamic LP fee FLOOR..CEILING from the token's section, owner-snapshotted via syncFee, beforeInitialize refusing non-dynamic-fee pools). src/V4PositionPlanner.sol is a read-only Solidity encoder returning canonical PositionManager modifyLiquidities action plans (MINT_POSITION+SETTLE_PAIR etc.) so the client never needs an ABI coder; src/Venue.sol is a stateless, write-free, defensively-read Uniswap v3 reader (gas-stipended staticcalls, hand-decoded observe, factory() cross-check, router calldata shape pinned beside the router address). All hooks have only ever executed against test/mocks/MockPoolManager.sol (selector-faithful, OVERRIDE_FEE-aware, permission-bits-aware), never a real v4 PoolManager.

The UI is served from chain twice: the token's own tokenURI HTML (engine/ipseity.html, ~104 KB face 0, with its own keccak/ABI encoder and a Market instrument that quotes, trades, bonds, deposits, withdraws and syncs through a bytes-first propose() confirmation) reading the pool address from the window.IPSE state block the Renderer writes; and the ERC-5219 web3:// site (Premises -> PageMarket/PagePool/PageSwap/PageLaunch/PageHook, JS held as Solidity string constants in Desk/DeskUni/DeskTrade/DeskLaunch, every selector keccak'd on chain into a JSON config block, no keccak/ABI coder/floats in the browser). There is no authentication layer: reads are public, the client compares the EIP-6963-chosen account to ownerOf(id) as a courtesy gate, and the contracts enforce onlyHolder (Pool, strict ownerOf) / mayActAs (Kiln: owner or the token's ERC-6551 account, never a renter) / owner-only syncFee / launcher+mayActAs on mintPlan.

Two cautions for the merge: the whole market is unaudited (per-market maxDeposit cap, MAINNET_READINESS gates), and this reading found an unguarded re-entrancy path the repo sketched but never ran — a holder-controlled hostile ERC-20 can re-enter the unguarded closeMarket from inside deposit, leave stale reserves on a deleted market, re-open on another pair (openMarket never resets rBase/rQuote) and withdraw other markets' tokens when allowlistEnforced is false, which is how every testnet deployment was made. The fix is a global re-entrancy lock plus zeroing reserves on open.

components.name: Pool
components.purpose: One AMM per NFT in a single contract; ownerOf(id) is the sole LP and authority; anchored virtual-reserve constant product; ratcheting bond; unpausable withdrawal; enumerable open-market set.
key_functions: constructor(IIpseity collection_, uint256 maxDeposit_, address admin_, bool enforce)
openMarket(uint256 id, address base, address quote, uint16 feeBps) onlyHolder
closeMarket(uint256 id) onlyHolder (requires unbonded and both reserves zero)
setFee(uint256 id, uint16 feeBps) onlyHolder (<= 500 bps, refused while bonded)
bond(uint256 id, uint64 until) onlyHolder (RatchetOnly, BondTooLong > 365d)
deposit(uint256 id, uint256 amountBase, uint256 amountQuote) onlyHolder nonReentrant notPaused (credits what arrived; cap per side added to)
withdraw(uint256 id, uint256 amountBase, uint256 amountQuote, address to) onlyHolder nonReentrant (never pausable; refused while bonded)
quote(uint256 id, bool baseIn, uint256 amountIn) view returns (uint256)
swap(uint256 id, bool baseIn, uint256 amountIn, uint256 minOut, address to, uint256 deadline) before(deadline) nonReentrant notPaused returns (uint256 out)
syncCurve(uint256 id) onlyHolder (copies sectionOf(id); refused while bonded)
pendingCurve(uint256 id) view returns (bool drifted, uint256 nowBps, uint256 wouldBeBps)
market(uint256 id) view returns 12 values incl. maxBaseOut/maxQuoteOut (output caps) and bondUntil
openCount() / openIds(uint256 from, uint256 count)
setPaused(bool) / bless(address,bool) / setAllowlistEnforced(bool) / proposeAdmin(address) / acceptAdmin() onlyAdmin
design_decisions: Market keyed by token id; ownerOf is the LP so selling the NFT sells the exchange — 'the whole reason this is a separate contract keyed by token id rather than a fork of Uniswap with an NFT bolted on'.
No LP shares, no oracle/TWAP, no flash loans — deliberately absent; single provider removes share accounting and first-depositor attacks at the cost of aggregation.
Curve is a COPY of the section word, not a live read, because an ERC-4907 renter may operate the artwork and must not reprice someone else's inventory.
Offsets vBase/vQuote are ANCHORED (written only on liquidity/curve change, never by a trade); deriving them per quote let a round trip extract 400 -> 718.
The bond ratchets, survives transfer, freezes exits and terms, keeps additive ops open; _reanchor is a no-op under a live bond (invariant 56).
Pause halts trading and deposits only; withdrawal has no pause modifier — 'a pause that traps money is a slower theft'.
MAX_OUT_BPS=5000: the curve prices against liquidity it does not hold, so the pool states its maximum trade rather than promising what it cannot pay.
minOut is checked against the measured balance delta at the recipient (fee-on-transfer output cannot defeat the floor).
Deposit cap bounds only the side being deposited into (both-sides check locked bonded holders out).
market() reports concentration 0 for unopened markets because word 0's offset is the far edge of w (6.37x misreport fixed).
Enumerable set via push/swap-and-pop so a directory finds markets on high ids without walking 4096 tokens.
security_invariants: INV15 (x+vx)(y+vy) never falls across a trade, measured against the stored offsets
INV16 a round trip never profits at any concentration up to 40% of reserve
INV16b a trade never moves the curve; every anchor write emits CurveAnchored
INV17 no payout over half the outgoing reserve
INV20/21 curve is a copy; only the holder moves inventory
INV22 selling the token sells the market
INV23/24 bond only ratchets, survives sale, <= 1 year
INV25/26 credited reserve is what arrived; floor applies to what the recipient receives
INV27/28/29 no admin path can move an asset (ABI-proven); pause never traps money; two-step admin
INV56 bond freezes the curve through every door including deposit
INV62 deposit cap only on the side added to
INV63 two markets on one token never over-claim — a MONITOR only (tools/agents.mjs); bless is the defence
standards: declares ERC-4907 userOf but never uses it
components.reuse_notes: Core design is exactly the GOAL's swap-inside-the-NFT. Must add a global re-entrancy lock (closeMarket/openMarket/setFee/bond/syncCurve are unguarded; holder-controlled hostile token can re-enter closeMarket from deposit, leave stale reserves, re-open on another pair and drain — see report section 13.1), zero reserves on openMarket, read offsets before _pull in swap, make the concentration source pluggable (today hard-wired to sectionOf), re-point IIpseity at the unified hub, decide whether the token's ERC-6551 account may act as holder (Kiln admits it, Pool does not), consider native-ETH pairs. Runtime 11,626 B.

components.name: Curve
components.purpose: Pricing library: concentration(word) in bps from the 4-D section (cut-plane normal + per-solid measured slice tables), anchor(), amountOut(), spot(), invariant().
key_functions: cutDirection(uint256 word) pure returns (int256 ux, int256 uy, int256 uz, int256 uw) — u = R·e_w closed form in 1e9 fixed point
concentration(uint256 word) pure returns (uint256 bps) — 0 at rest .. MAX_CONCENTRATION 80_000
anchor(uint256 word, uint256 rBase, uint256 rQuote) pure returns (uint256 vBase, uint256 vQuote)
amountOut(uint256 amountIn, uint256 rIn, uint256 rOut, uint256 vIn, uint256 vOut, uint256 feeBps) pure returns (uint256)
spot(rIn, rOut, vIn, vOut) pure returns (uint256) scaled 1e18
invariant(rIn, rOut, vIn, vOut) pure returns (uint256)
design_decisions: Constant product with a change of origin: inherits CPMM's monotone/convex proof for every committable rotation.
Deviation from rest, not slice size: a tesseract cut square is its SMALLEST slice, so 'thin section, tight market' would open fresh tesseracts at max concentration; rest = 0 bps on every solid.
Function of the cut plane u, not of the angles: half a turn in two w-planes returns the same plane; the old sum-of-angles priced an untouched picture at 5.33x/8x.
Sixteen direction cells x four offsets per solid, measured off the engine's distance functions (R^2 0.86 Tesseract via max|u_i|, 0.81 Ditorus via u_z^2+u_w^2; 24-cell isotropic).
Rounding toward the pool (yNew rounded up); fee off the priced input but whole input lands in reserves so k rises every trade.
security_invariants: concentration bounded [0, 80000]
non-w planes never move the price
more in never means less out
quote never exceeds priced reserve
contract's cut direction matches the engine's rot4 to 1e-6
components.reuse_notes: anchor/amountOut/spot/invariant reusable verbatim for any virtual-reserve CPMM; concentration(word) with SLICE (128 B) / FALLOFF (32 B) tables only if the unified token keeps IPSEITY's 4-D section; otherwise keep the signature and feed it another per-token signal.

components.name: Venue
components.purpose: Stateless, write-free reader of Uniswap v3 (factory/quoter/router/positions/wrapped/governor/v4 PoolManager/v4 Positions/Permit2 as a Wiring struct); comparison on token market pages and the generic /swap page.
key_functions: constructor(Wiring memory w) — UnknownRouterKind if routerKind > 1
present() / hasV4() view
tiers() pure returns uint24[4] [100,500,3000,10000]; enabled(uint24) / spacings() read from the factory
best(address base, address quote, uint8 baseDecimals) view returns (Look) — deepest by in-range liquidity
survey(base, quote, baseDecimals) view returns (Look[4])
poolAt(address a, address b, uint24 fee) view; state(address pool) view returns (PoolState) with factory() cross-check
history(address pool, uint32 window, uint8 points) view returns (bool ok, int24[] ticks, uint32 step) — hand-decoded observe
oldest(address pool) view returns (bool ok, uint32 secondsAgo)
sqrtAt(int24) / priceAt(int24, uint256 unit, bool baseIsToken0) / spacing(uint24) / usable(int24, int24) pure
design_decisions: Only reads; every write goes from the visitor's wallet straight to Uniswap.
Router KIND stored beside the router address: the two exactInputSingle shapes differ by one word and the wrong one shifts recipient and every amount without reverting.
All seven addresses are constructor arguments and every page prints them (v3 addresses differ on Base).
Raw staticcalls with gas stipends (60k/40k/2M); abi.decode avoided on attacker-chosen lengths; price and tick sanity-checked.
history window trimmed to whole steps (newest bar was mis-scaled before).
security_invariants: no function moves anything
INV98 router calldata shape travels with its address
standards: reads Uniswap v3 core/periphery (IUniswapV3Factory, IUniswapV3Pool, QuoterV2 via eth_call only)
components.reuse_notes: Optional for the GOAL (external venue comparison / generic swap page). Chain-agnostic; re-verify per-chain wiring (tools/site.mjs UNISWAP table). Runtime 8,245 B.

Mul.mulDiv(uint256 a, uint256 b, uint256 d) pure

floor property
reciprocal pricing within 1e12

components.name: Coin
components.purpose: Fixed-supply ERC-20 with no mint, burn-from, pause, blacklist, owner or upgrade path; whole supply minted to the launcher at deployment.
key_functions: constructor(string n, string s, uint8 d, uint256 supply, address to)
transfer / approve / transferFrom (infinite-allowance short circuit)

components.name: Kiln
components.purpose: The launchpad: CREATE2 coin deployment signed by a collection token, view-mined v4 hook salts, hook deployment with permission-bit verification, Facet band preview and arg packing.
key_functions: mayActAs(uint256 token, address who) view — owner or the token's ERC-6551 account, never a renter
launch(uint256 token, string name_, string symbol_, uint8 decimals_, uint256 supply, bytes32 salt) returns (address coin) — salt' = keccak256(abi.encode(msg.sender, salt))
coinAt(address by, string, string, uint8, uint256, bytes32) view returns (address)
coinCount() / recent(uint256 from, uint256 count) newest first
mine(bytes32 initCodeHash, uint16 flags, uint256 from, uint256 tries) view returns (bool found, bytes32 salt, address at)
deployHook(uint8 kind, bytes32 salt, bytes32 arg) returns (address hook) — reverts WrongFlags(wanted, got)
band(uint256 token, uint24 floor_, uint24 ceiling_) view returns (uint256 section, uint256 concentration, uint24 feeNow)
facetArg(uint256 token, uint24 floor_, uint24 ceiling_) pure returns (bytes32) — token<<48 | floor<<24 | ceiling
recipeHash(uint8 kind, bytes32 arg) view returns (bytes32 hash, uint16 flags)
design_decisions: The expensive keccak-shaped part of deploying a hook is a read under eth_call, so a keccak-less client can do it; windows of 60,000 because eth_call has a gas ceiling.
flags must match EXACTLY (a spare bit means a callback the hook does not implement).
Sender mixed into the salt defeats mempool front-running of the address.
The contract that unpacks the Facet arg is the one that packs it (off-by-eight puts the token id in the fee band silently).
v4 structs declared locally for selector identity; no privileged caller anywhere; POOL_MANAGER is a constructor argument.
security_invariants: INV100 a hook's permissions are its address and the kiln refuses a mismatch
one mined salt gives the same hook address on every chain (CREATE2 has no chain id)
components.reuse_notes: Re-point IHolds at the unified hub; decide raise mechanics (none here — liquidity goes straight to v4 via the planner); record pool keys per coin; remove dead AlreadyLaunched. Runtime 13,709 B. Deployed on Sepolia 0x29de13b7… and Base Sepolia 0x2daaf1c6…

components.name: Gate
components.purpose: v4 hook: beforeSwap reverts NotOpenYet before OPENS; beforeRemoveLiquidity reverts StillLocked before UNLOCKS; both immutable; status() for pages.
key_functions: constructor(address manager, uint64 opens, uint64 unlocks)
beforeSwap(address, PoolKey, SwapParams, bytes) view onlyManager returns (bytes4, int256, uint24)
beforeRemoveLiquidity(address, PoolKey, ModifyLiquidityParams, bytes) view onlyManager returns (bytes4)
status() view returns (bool tradingOpen, bool liquidityFree)
design_decisions: Ignores every argument but the clock — fewer fields to be wrong about
Returns zero fee override because a nonzero override on a non-dynamic pool reverts
'These are exactly the bits a trap has' — safety comes from immutability, not address shape
security_invariants: executed through a selector-faithful MockPoolManager: shut, open, still locked, released; adding liquidity never gated
standards: Uniswap v4 IHooks subset by selector
components.reuse_notes: 1,008 B. Never executed against a real PoolManager; pitfall: a dynamic-fee pool behind a Gate charges zero forever (page guard exists).

components.name: Facet
components.purpose: v4 dynamic-fee hook: LP fee = FLOOR + (CEILING-FLOOR) * Curve.concentration(section)/80000 where section is an owner-approved snapshot of the token's 4-D section; beforeInitialize refuses non-dynamic pools.
key_functions: constructor(address manager, IHubSection hub, uint256 token, uint24 floor_, uint24 ceiling_)
section() view
syncFee() — msg.sender must be HUB.ownerOf(TOKEN)
fee() view returns (uint24)
reading() view returns (section, concentration, now, floor, ceiling)
beforeInitialize(address, PoolKey key, uint160) view onlyManager — NotDynamic unless key.fee == 0x800000
beforeSwap(...) view onlyManager returns (selector, 0, fee() | OVERRIDE_FEE)
flags() pure returns BEFORE_INITIALIZE | BEFORE_SWAP
design_decisions: A fee, not a custom curve: beforeSwapReturnDelta would make the hook responsible for the invariant with no backstop; a fee bug is bounded by an immutable band.
Owner snapshot (commit 375917e) so an ERC-4907 renter cannot move the fee — same lesson as Pool.syncCurve.
BEFORE_INITIALIZE exists solely to refuse a pool whose key would discard the override in silence.
security_invariants: at rest the pool charges exactly FLOOR on every solid
renter cannot move or sync the fee
a fee returned without OVERRIDE_FEE is ignored by the manager — the mock reproduces this
standards: Uniswap v4 IHooks subset; LPFeeLibrary DYNAMIC_FEE_FLAG/OVERRIDE_FEE_FLAG reproduced
components.reuse_notes: Keep only with a per-token on-chain signal; otherwise drop. 3,722 B. No public-chain deployment recorded.

components.name: Hook library
components.purpose: v4 flag constants reproduced from v4-core Hooks.sol, DYNAMIC_FEE/OVERRIDE_FEE/MAX_FEE, address readers (flags, has, inert, touchesSwaps, guardsExits), plain-English name/meaning per bit, CREATE2 address.

inert(address) / touchesSwaps(address) / guardsExits(address) pure
name(uint256 i) / meaning(uint256 i) / bit(uint256 i) pure

unique_ideas: One AMM per NFT keyed by token id with ownerOf as the sole LP: selling the NFT sells the exchange, no LP shares, no migration.

Ratcheting bond (bondUntil only moves out, <= 365 days, survives transfer) freezing every exit and term while deposits and trades stay open — the mechanism that makes the market a promise a buyer can read on chain.

Anchored virtual reserves written only on liquidity/curve change, never by a trade, with a CurveAnchored event as the audit signal; the fuzz property that caught the derived-per-quote leak (400 -> 718).
Curve copy vs live read (syncCurve/pendingCurve) so an ERC-4907 renter cannot reprice someone else's inventory; same lesson applied to Facet.syncFee.
Admin that provably cannot move assets (asserted against the compiled ABI), withdrawal that can never be paused, two-step admin.
Enumerable open-market set (openCount/openIds) and a token list DERIVED from open markets instead of fetched.
Mining v4 hook salts inside a view (Kiln.mine) so a keccak-less browser deploys hooks under eth_call; sender-mixed salts; WrongFlags check after deploy; one salt = same hook address on every chain.
/hook/<address>: a contract-rendered inspector of a hook's fourteen permission bits with the 'a lock and a trap have the same address shape' caveat.
Facet: an LP fee driven by an on-chain per-token word (the artwork), owner-snapshotted, with beforeInitialize refusing non-dynamic pools and Kiln.band() previewing the exact fee the hook will charge.
V4PositionPlanner: a read-only Solidity ABI encoder for nested PositionManager action plans so the client never needs an ABI coder and never grants the planner an approval.
Measured transfers on both sides so fee-on-transfer tokens cannot overstate reserves or defeat minOut.
Venue's defensive reading: gas-stipended staticcalls, hand-decoded dynamic returns against offset bombs, factory() cross-check, router calldata shape pinned beside the router address.
On-chain selector computation into JSON config blocks and a browser client with no keccak, no ABI coder and no floating point.
Site-driving tests that mount the served HTML, execute the served JS against a DOM shim and the in-process EVM, and assert on balances.
weaknesses: FOUND, UNRESOLVED: closeMarket/openMarket/setFee/bond/syncCurve carry no re-entrancy guard; a holder that is also a hostile ERC-20 (test/mocks/PoolReenter.sol, unreferenced; tools/poc-pool.mjs is an unfinished 512-byte stub) can re-enter closeMarket from inside deposit (reserves still zero), have deposit write rBase into the deleted struct, re-open on a different pair (openMarket never resets rBase/rQuote) and withdraw other markets' tokens. Precondition: allowlistEnforced false or the token blessed — testnet deployments pass enforce=false and admin=deployer EOA.

FOUND: swap reads vIn/vOut after _pull, so a holder-controlled callback token can syncCurve (unguarded) mid-pull and re-anchor the curve the trade is about to use; bounded by minOut but makes weakness B atomic.
Unaudited money code; per-market maxDeposit cap; MAINNET_READINESS blocks on stateful invariant campaigns, audit, multisig+timelock, bug bounty.
B (repo-stated): holder can reshape an unbonded curve against a pending trade; minOut is the only protection.
63 (repo-stated): two markets sharing one ERC-20 balance can over-claim with rebasing/fee/sweeping tokens; a monitor only; bless is the defence and is a centralisation trade-off.
Single LP per market, no aggregation, no oracle/TWAP; ERC-20 pairs only (no native ETH).
Pool.onlyHolder excludes operators and the token's own ERC-6551 account (inconsistent with Kiln.mayActAs).

Gate/Facet have only executed against MockPoolManager ('It is not v4'); no Facet/Gate deployment on a public chain is recorded; v4 Actions/flag constants are hand-copied and must be re-verified per release.
/swap is single-hop; SwapRouter02 deployments have no reachable deadline; QuoterV2 quotes depend on the wallet's node running a 30M-gas eth_call.

website_delivery: Entirely from chain, two surfaces. (1) Ipseity.tokenURI(id) -> Renderer -> JSON whose animation_url is the whole WebGL2 app as a nested data: URI; the HTML lives as SSTORE2 gzip shards (39,501 B on chain for a 113,379 B minified document) and tokenURI writes window.IPSE={id, collection, chainId, owner, account, grip, reachImpl, gripImpl, pool, seed, word, ...} between head and body; the Market instrument (engine/ipseity.html:3371-3655) reads Pool.market/quote/pendingCurve by eth_call through the injected EIP-1193 provider and builds swap/openMarket/deposit/withdraw/bond/syncCurve calldata with its own keccak/ABI encoder, showing decoded bytes in propose() before eth_sendTransaction. (2) The ERC-5219 site: Premises.request answers web3://<premises>:<chainId>/{token/<id>/market, token/<id>/pool, open[/n], swap, launch, hook/<addr>}; pages are Solidity string builders; page JS is Solidity string constants (Chrome.WALLET_JS, Desk.CORE_JS/POOL_JS/SWAP_JS, DeskUni.BASE_JS, DeskTrade.SWAP_JS, DeskLaunch.LAUNCH_JS); every selector is keccak256(signature) computed on chain into <script type=application/json id=D|K>; the browser pads words only (no keccak, no ABI coder, no floats). An HTTP gateway (tools/gateway.mjs, w3link) is a convenience where every GET is an eth_call; nothing is fetched from IPFS or a server.
wallet_gating: No authentication layer; reads are public ('The gate is a courtesy, not a secret ... What ownership actually gates is writing, and that is gated by the contract', Chrome.sol:177-180). Client side: EIP-6963 announcers are collected and one is chosen (stored choice / only wallet / picker), the chain is checked, and the holder test is connected account == ownerOf(id) — the instrument re-reads ownerOf on every refresh and needOwner() throws before building holder-only calldata; the site toggles body.held/.gate/.only CSS and PagePool prints the holder with a note that the contract will refuse others. Contract side (the real enforcement): Pool.onlyHolder is strict ownerOf == msg.sender (no operators, no ERC-6551 account, no ERC-4907 user); Kiln.mayActAs admits the owner OR the token's ERC-6551 account (so Reach session keys can launch) and never a renter; Facet.syncFee is owner-only; V4PositionPlanner.mintPlan requires launcher == msg.sender and mayActAs. Delegation exists only through the ERC-6551 Reach's session keys (expiry, spend cap, target+selector allowlists). Renters are excluded from every money path by design (invariants 13, 20, 21; commit 375917e).

pitfalls: Virtual reserves derived from live reserves re-anchor the curve per trade: k conserved within a trade, not across two; 400 in -> 718 out. Store the offsets; write them only on liquidity/curve change.
deposit re-anchored the curve under a live bond (claim 1 -> INV56): every door that moves a term must be frozen, including the additive ones.
Deposit cap checked on the untouched side locked a bonded holder out of every function (claim 13 -> INV62).
maxBaseIn/maxQuoteIn were output caps; the instrument compared the input against the near side's cap (INV65).
market()/pendingCurve() priced non-existent markets at 6.37x: section word 0's offset is the far edge of w, the centre is 32768.
Test fixtures certified the old curve: a half turn in two w-planes is the same cut plane as rest; a fuzz property that asserted the implementation rather than a property hid it.

The v4 hooks had never executed; callbacks are matched BY SELECTOR so a type drift means 'never called'; a returned fee without OVERRIDE_FEE is silently ignored; 'pretty' test addresses already carry permission bits (0xef..00 asserts BEFORE_INITIALIZE); trailing bytes offsets were 7 words instead of 9/10 and the swap case passed by accident; mine returns three words, recipeHash two.
Dynamic fee + Gate = a pool priced at zero forever and unrepairable (pool key immutable); the page guard asked !mined instead of mined.sets and deployHook was hard-coded to kind 0.
A const in the temporal dead zone killed every button on /launch while six regex assertions on the served text passed — run the served JS, do not only grep it.

Two Uniswap routers' exactInputSingle differ by one word and the wrong shape does not revert; QuoterV2's NatSpec parameter order differs from its struct; SwapRouter02 amountIn=0 is the CONTRACT_BALANCE sentinel; recipients 0x1/0x2 are sentinels; negative ticks need two's-complement words.

Hostile ERC-20s on market pages: script-tag symbol(), bytes32 symbols (MKR), 200 decimals, 8 KB answers, ABI offsets pointing megabytes past the buffer (2,151M gas in the page frame — the staticcall stipend protects nothing).
Venue.history must trim the window to whole steps or the newest bar is scaled wrong.
BORN_OPEN shipped as 0x587 (money panel open, picture sealed) and a suite assertion pinned the wrong constant.
Unguarded closeMarket + openMarket not resetting reserves = cross-market drain with a holder-controlled token when the allowlist is off (this review); swap reads offsets after _pull.
The PoC scaffolding for the above (test/mocks/PoolReenter.sol, tools/poc-pool.mjs) was committed unfinished and unreferenced — scaffolding that looks like a test is not a test.
